skill.name: verify-and-stop
skill.description: Prove existing work meets acceptance conditions without expanding scope. Use for validation-only tasks, completion checks, focused gate runs, and last-mile proof.
skill.summary: Verify acceptance criteria with the smallest sufficient proof set, report unresolved risks, and stop when the requested evidence is complete.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: The skill contains only concise instructions for scoped verification and reporting. No static findings, prompt injection attempts, harmful intent, or semantic security risks were found.

content.value_statement: Verification tasks often expand beyond their acceptance criteria. This skill selects sufficient checks, reports exact outcomes, and stops when proof is complete.
actual_capabilities: Translates acceptance conditions into a minimal proof set.
Reuses current results when they match the repository state.
Runs focused checks before broader verification gates.
Classifies outcomes as pass, fail, unavailable, or blocked.
Reports commands, results, and unresolved risks.
Stops after sufficient acceptance evidence is collected.
limitations: Does not define acceptance criteria when none are provided.
Does not fix product code unless the request includes fixes.
Cannot run checks that are unavailable in the current environment.
Does not add unrelated cleanup, polish, or tests.

use_cases.title: Confirm a focused change
use_cases.description: Validate a small implementation against explicit acceptance criteria without extending the task.

use_cases.title: Review completion evidence
use_cases.description: Check whether reported commands and results sufficiently prove a ticket is complete.

use_cases.title: Run release gates
use_cases.description: Execute relevant checks in increasing scope and report any remaining release risk.

prompt_templates.title: Verify one criterion
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this acceptance criterion: [criterion]. Run the smallest sufficient check, report the result, and stop.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs proof for one clear requirement.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a completed task
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify [task] against these criteria: [criteria]. Reuse current evidence where valid, then run focused missing checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants a concise completion check.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an existing report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this verification evidence: [evidence]. Identify unsupported criteria, run only necessary checks, and classify each outcome exactly.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer needs to assess whether existing evidence is sufficient.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a release candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate [release candidate] against [gates]. Start with focused checks, expand only when required, and report unresolved risks before stopping.
prompt_templates.scenario: A release engineer needs controlled, risk-based verification.

output_examples.input: Verify that the updated parser accepts empty input and preserves existing valid cases.
output_examples.output: Pass. The focused empty-input test and existing parser suite passed. Acceptance evidence is complete. No unresolved risk was identified.

output_examples.input: Confirm the deployment is ready, but the required integration service is unavailable.
output_examples.output: Blocked. Local checks passed, but the required integration check could not run because the service was unavailable. Deployment readiness remains unproven.

output_examples.input: Review completion using test results from an earlier repository state.
output_examples.output: Unavailable evidence. The results do not match the current repository state. Fresh focused checks are required before completion can be confirmed.

best_practices: Provide explicit, testable acceptance criteria before verification begins.
Keep repository state stable while collecting and reporting evidence.
Record exact commands, outcomes, and unresolved risks.
anti_patterns: Do not broaden verification into unrelated cleanup or feature work.
Do not treat stale results as proof for a changed repository.
Do not claim success when required checks are unavailable or blocked.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It verifies existing work against supplied acceptance conditions using the smallest sufficient set of checks.

faq.question: Will it modify product code?
faq.answer: It avoids product code changes unless the verification request explicitly includes fixes.

faq.question: Can it reuse previous test results?
faq.answer: Yes, when those results are current and match the repository state being verified.

faq.question: How does it report failed checks?
faq.answer: It distinguishes pass, fail, unavailable, and blocked outcomes and reports unresolved risk.

faq.question: Does it run the full test suite first?
faq.answer: No. It starts with focused checks and uses broader gates only when needed.

faq.question: When does verification stop?
faq.answer: It stops when every acceptance condition has sufficient evidence or a blocking limitation is clearly reported.
